Command acceptance returns receipts after persistence; provider work is performed by a worker outside the acceptance transaction. Worker recovery and undo state are durable. The sync service owns the Gmail cache and coordinates provider reads and queued operations. SQLite transactions persist local state; network calls occur through the provider path. [gmail/provider.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/provider.rs) owns HTTP, credentials, pacing, status, and quota handling; [gmail/provider/api.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/provider/api.rs) implements the `GmailProvider` trait (auth/session, reads and writes; defined in [gmail/types.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/types.rs)) for the concrete `LiveGmailProvider`; [gmail/parse.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/parse.rs) contains pure Gmail response and message parsing. OAuth flow, token access, and secret storage are in [gmail/auth.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/auth.rs) and [gmail/secrets.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/secrets.rs). layouts, so only those historical migration bodies inspect optional columns.
An already-current profile performs no migration writes. Fresh profiles use the
canonical schema captured from the pre-change store. Unknown or newer markers
fail before schema changes. Startup crash recovery runs explicitly after
migration: globally applying operations become uncertain and lose `last_error`.
Reconnect recovery remains account-scoped and additionally clears `failure`;
these distinct semantics are preserved.

# Development guide

This repository contains two deliberately separate native profiles: a durable
synthetic fixture profile and an explicit Gmail profile built in stages. Slice 01
describes the fixture baseline; the current core also includes Gmail OAuth, cache,
sync, and provider operations.
Slice 02 adds system-browser OAuth/PKCE, a macOS Keychain credential store,
bounded inbox caching, and background sync. Slice 03 adds opt-in, durable Gmail
archive/unarchive and explicit read/unread actions; Gmail remains read-only until
the user explicitly requests the broader Google `gmail.modify` permission.
Slice 04 adds a local-only plain-text composer and durable draft recovery, but
still does not send/delete mail or expose arbitrary labels. Opening a message
never marks it read. UX-05 adds bounded multi-select and durable bulk
archive/read group processing with one-level partial group Undo; the browser
preview remains synthetic and in-memory. See
the slice contracts for individual acceptance scope. UX-08 adds narrow Gmail-mode
Star/Unstar singles/groups, durable Undo/reconciliation, cache-only Starred and a
single cached starred filter; see [its contract and validation ledger](ux-08-stars.md).
The legacy native fixture remains archive-only for mailbox operations; unsupported
star controls are absent there. Reminders use local device storage in both native
profiles. No real provider writes are authorized by implementation tests.

## UX-09 increment A: read-only provider mail

The **Provider mail** rail entry (Gmail native or labelled browser preview) opens
a bounded destination browser for Sent, provider Drafts, All Mail, Spam, Trash
and user labels. Search covers the loaded catalog; Show more expands it. It is
not mailbox search. All Mail excludes Spam/Trash. Every page contains at most
25 conversations, at most 16 MiB of serialized thread DTOs, and no exact total.
Catalog and page rows are real buttons with one roving tab stop: ArrowDown/ArrowUp
or J/K move between rows, Enter opens, and Escape steps back one level (reader,
page list, catalog) before it closes the drawer. Errors use the same plain
sentences as the Account drawer, never a raw error kind.
The read-only drawer intentionally has no triage/reply controls. Its page remains
mounted during a reader visit; closing the drawer returns to the prior inbox
context. This is not yet the roadmap's integrated main-list destination context.

Native commands `list_provider_destinations(accountId, cached)` and
`browse_provider_destination(request)` run off the UI thread, require the active
account, and use readonly Gmail APIs. Page cursors carry account+destination
identity and a bounded opaque provider token; they grant no authority.
A separate SQLite table retains one catalog and up to 20 destination snapshots
(latest successful page per retained destination), independent of inbox discovery,
history and operation recovery. **Use saved catalog/page** is explicit and
timestamped; provider failures are never silently converted to saved success or
an empty list. Restart retains these snapshots; disconnect clears them.

Provider Drafts are read-only snapshots, **not** the app's local editable drafts.
The native fixture rejects both provider commands; browser preview models them
in memory only. Label/Move, label badges on ordinary inbox rows, palette integration,
and saved-view/search criteria are not implemented here. This increment preserves
and coexists with the current UX-06/07/08 implementations. See
[the increment contract](ux-09-provider-destinations.md)
for evidence and remaining gates.

### Safe bulk selection and processing (UX-05)

Conversations can be selected in the Inbox/Done list with `X`, `Shift+J/K`,
Cmd/Ctrl-click, Shift-click ranges and per-row labelled checkboxes, bounded to
100 selected conversations per action (additive ranges; Select all loaded is
disabled with an explanation beyond the bound; selection clears on
context/account changes and survives reader visits with a visible bulk-scope
banner). Shared toolbar, palette and shortcut actions apply to the whole
selection when one exists (group path, even for one row); inline row actions
stay row-scoped, and Reply/open/navigation are never bulk.

A bulk action accepts one durable **operation group**: structure, duplicates,
bounds, request ID, active account and capability are validated before a single
SQLite transaction persists the group header, immutable per-member targets and
preimages, and per-member acceptance results. A gone/unactionable member becomes
a persisted typed rejection, not a fabricated failed provider operation;
all-rejected valid requests get an idempotent receipt and consume no Undo slot.
Same-request replays (including after restart) return the original receipt;
changed payloads are `request_id_conflict`. Archive/unarchive groups work in
fixture and Gmail mode; read/unread groups are Gmail-only, like the single
setters.

`Z` within the 10-second Rust-clock window undoes the latest top-level action,
whether a single or a group. A group Undo makes one durable attempt: queued
members are cancelled, applying/confirmed members are compensated from the
original preimages, and ineligible members (failed, unknown outcome, unknown
prior, already undone, acceptance-rejected) are explicitly skipped with reasons.
Partial results are worded honestly: the dock line stays short ("Restored 1 · 1
skipped — failed"; skips are named only when there are some) while its title and
accessible description keep the exact ledger ("Undo accepted for 1 of 2; 1
skipped (1 failed); …"), and per-member failures stay recoverable in Activity regardless of
current list rows. A rejected IPC acceptance is never treated as "nothing
happened": the UI keeps the original request ID and recovers via
`get_operation_group` / replay of the exact original request.

Browser-preview group behavior is modelled by the labelled in-memory fake, which
continues to disclose that it is non-durable; it makes no provider or storage
calls.

1	# Current architecture
2	
3	**Scope:** This is an inventory of architecture that exists in the source tree. It describes code paths and ownership. For feature availability and validation results, see [current status](current-status.md). For the selected first-build scope, see [ADR 0001](adr/0001-single-account-desktop-email-client.md). [ARCHITECTURE.md](../ARCHITECTURE.md) is a historical proposal; its design recommendations are not evidence of implementation.
4	
5	## Runtime and boundaries
6	
7	The app has a Vue/TypeScript frontend, a Tauri 2 shell, and the Rust `mail-core` crate. The Rust crate owns persistence and provider operations. The frontend talks through a `MailClient` interface. In native mode, `createTauriMailClient` maps that interface to named Tauri commands. In browser mode, `browser-fake.ts` supplies a synthetic in-memory client. The shared interface and generated wire types are in [client.ts](../src/lib/ipc/client.ts), [tauri-client.ts](../src/lib/ipc/tauri-client.ts), [browser-fake.ts](../src/lib/ipc/browser-fake.ts), and [generated.ts](../src/lib/ipc/generated.ts). Rust DTOs are the source for generated TypeScript; `crates/mail-core/src/bin/generate-types.rs` generates the file.
8	
9	The Tauri entry point in [main.rs](../src-tauri/src/main.rs) selects fixture or Gmail mode from configuration, opens the corresponding Rust store, registers command handlers, and emits mailbox/draft/close events. The webview does not access SQLite or provider HTTP directly. Its capabilities and generated command permissions are under [src-tauri/capabilities](../src-tauri/capabilities/main-window.json) and [src-tauri/permissions/autogenerated](../src-tauri/permissions/autogenerated).
10	
11	## Rust state and transaction ownership
12	
13	The fixture `MailCore` in [lib.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/lib.rs) owns a SQLite-backed `Store`, profile lock, change listeners, and a serial archive worker. [store.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/store.rs) owns fixture persistence and transaction logic. Command acceptance returns receipts after persistence; provider work is performed by a worker outside the acceptance transaction. Worker recovery and undo state are durable. The fixture provider is synthetic and does not connect to a mail service.
14	
15	Gmail mode is implemented separately in [gmail/sync.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/sync.rs), [gmail/store.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/store.rs), [gmail/operations.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/operations.rs), and the Gmail provider modules. The sync service owns the Gmail cache and coordinates provider reads and queued operations. SQLite transactions persist local state; network calls occur through the provider path. [gmail/provider.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/provider.rs) owns HTTP, credentials, pacing, status, and quota handling; [gmail/provider/api.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/provider/api.rs) implements the `GmailProvider` trait (auth/session, reads and writes; defined in [gmail/types.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/types.rs)) for the concrete `LiveGmailProvider`; [gmail/parse.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/parse.rs) contains pure Gmail response and message parsing. OAuth flow, token access, and secret storage are in [gmail/auth.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/auth.rs) and [gmail/secrets.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/secrets.rs). The service exposes account status and sync state through DTOs. Runtime success on a supported macOS installation is a separate validation question; see [current status](current-status.md).
16	
17	Gmail schema upgrades are owned by `gmail/store_schema.rs`. The authoritative
18	`meta.schema_version` advances through `gmail-migrations-1` to
19	`gmail-migrations-9`, with each stage's DDL, backfills and marker in one
20	transaction. Pre-numbered `gmail-1` and `gmail-2` profiles had ambiguous physical
21	layouts, so only those historical migration bodies inspect optional columns.
22	An already-current profile performs no migration writes. Fresh profiles use the
23	canonical schema captured from the pre-change store. Unknown or newer markers
24	fail before schema changes. Startup crash recovery runs explicitly after
25	migration: globally applying operations become uncertain and lose `last_error`.
26	Reconnect recovery remains account-scoped and additionally clears `failure`;
27	these distinct semantics are preserved.
28	
29	`GmailStore` stays one type owning the single SQLite connection; its impl and
30	helpers are split by responsibility under `gmail/store/`. `store.rs` holds the
31	shared types and the struct; every method that opens a transaction still opens
32	exactly one, so acceptance and reconciliation keep their atomic scope.
33	
34	| Module | Responsibility |
35	| --- | --- |
36	| `profile` | open and startup recovery, account identity, generation, sync checkpoints, disconnect cleanup, saved split |
37	| `cache`, `cache_rows` | cached conversation reads; thread and fact upserts, eviction, conversation building, `meta` helpers |
38	| `ingestion` | discovery and history pages, rediscovery |
39	| `search`, `search_support` | cached search, done, trash and starred lists; search admission and eviction |
40	| `acceptance`, `operation_rows` | single-operation acceptance and retry; acceptance transaction, preimages, operation row codecs |
41	| `worker` | claim, confirm, reconcile, defer, requeue and finish |
42	| `undo`, `undo_support` | single-operation undo and its compensation helpers |
43	| `group_acceptance`, `group_queries`, `group_undo`, `group_rows` | group acceptance, status queries, group undo and the shared group row helpers |
44	| `activity` | effective conversation state and the activity list |
45	| `reminders`, `destinations` | local reminders; destination snapshots |
46	
47	Store tests live in `gmail/store_tests.rs` beside `migration_tests.rs`.
48	
49	Storage failures are diagnosable without leaking data. Every storage failure
50	still reaches the wire as `MailError::StorageUnavailable`, unchanged, but the
51	point that produced it first logs exactly one line through the `log` facade:
52	the call site's `file:line`, a static cause tag (`sqlite`, `lock_poisoned`,
53	`thread_join`, `path_unavailable`, `missing_persisted_row` and similar) and,
54	for SQLite errors, the primary result code name and extended code. The line
55	is built only from static strings and numbers; the Display text of the
56	underlying error is never read, because SQLite messages can quote values and
57	SQL. `mail-core` owns the helper in [storage_log.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/storage_log.rs);
58	the shell has its own small helper and the stderr logger in
59	[diagnostics.rs](../src-tauri/src/diagnostics.rs), which passes only the two
60	storage log targets and drops everything else. Re-mapping an error that was
61	already a `MailError` does not log a second time. Rejections because the sync
62	worker is stopped or halted are not logged: the failure that halted it already was.
63	
64	Drafts are stored in a separate `<selected-profile>/local-drafts` SQLite database by [drafts/store.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/drafts/store.rs), with revision and account identity types in [drafts/types.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/drafts/types.rs). The store uses WAL and FULL synchronous mode. Saves and deletes are revision-checked and return receipts after commit; deletion records request tombstones so a late save cannot recreate a removed draft. The frontend draft composable and editor coordinate local edits, acknowledged saves, and error recovery in [useDrafts.ts](../src/composables/useDrafts.ts), [DraftEditorCore.vue](../src/components/DraftEditorCore.vue), and [ReplyComposer.vue](../src/components/ReplyComposer.vue). Drafts remain local to the profile and do not sync to Gmail.
65	
66	The native close path uses a request/acknowledgement gate in [close_gate.rs](../src-tauri/src/close_gate.rs). The shell asks the frontend to flush and close dirty draft state; the frontend acknowledges only after the latest save is committed, and cancels close when save fails. Frontend coordination lives in [App.vue](../src/App.vue) and the draft composable. The governing contract is [vertical slice 04](vertical-slice-04.md).
67	
68	## Frontend coordination
69	
70	[App.vue](../src/App.vue) is the composition root for navigation, focused conversation, panels, and mailbox actions. [useMailbox.ts](../src/composables/useMailbox.ts) owns account-scoped focus and mailbox query coordination and keeps the public `Mailbox` shape. It composes focused modules that receive their dependencies as arguments rather than closing over the parent: [useMailboxSelection.ts](../src/composables/useMailboxSelection.ts) owns the UX-05 selection set, range anchor and `SELECTION_MAX` bound (the parent clears it on context, account and saved-view invalidation and prunes it after each authoritative list read), [useMailboxGroups.ts](../src/composables/useMailboxGroups.ts) owns UX-05 group dispatch, the single group notice, lost-response recovery on the original request id, partial group Undo, restart notice rehydration and the Activity group history/detail reads, [useMailboxDetailCache.ts](../src/composables/useMailboxDetailCache.ts) owns the bounded neighbor-detail cache, its TTL, the single-slot prefetch and the J/K reader loading delay (its fence is an epoch the owner bumps through `invalidateDetailCache()` on every refresh, mutation start, reader close, account change and disconnect), [useMailboxAccount.ts](../src/composables/useMailboxAccount.ts) owns authoritative account/mode status and the connect, disconnect, sync, enable-actions and cancel-upgrade lifecycle (each status read is fenced by its own request token and the session; it reports an account-identity change and a confirmed disconnect to `useMailbox` through callbacks, and `useMailbox` resets list, reader, group and selection state and bumps the session generation inside them), and [mailbox-refs.ts](../src/composables/mailbox-refs.ts) and [mailbox-session.ts](../src/composables/mailbox-session.ts) hold the shared conversation-reference helpers and the session/command-fence types. Session invalidation is an explicit argument: `useMailbox` owns the session counters and hands extracted pieces a read-only `MailboxSession` (generation and detached flag) plus the shared command fence; each async path captures the generation before its first await and drops its result when it moved. Components render the inbox, reader, composer, activity, and account controls. The client subscription events are invalidation hints; the frontend reloads through client queries.
71	
72	The production native client and browser fake share the same `MailClient` contract, but they do not share persistence or provider behavior. What is guaranteed to agree is the operation-ledger contract: shared scenario files in [tests/fixtures/contract-scenarios](../tests/fixtures/contract-scenarios) (acceptance, idempotent replay, undo, groups, typed errors) are executed by [contract_scenarios.rs](../crates/mail-core/tests/contract_scenarios.rs) against both Rust backends (`GmailCore` with the shared fake provider, and the fixture `MailCore` where it supports the scenario) and by [contract-scenarios.test.ts](../tests/browser-fake/contract-scenarios.test.ts) against the browser fake, with each side's own fake clock. Divergences that remain are named in the runners' `KNOWN_DIVERGENCES` tables and are still executed (they must fail), so they stay visible. Anything the scenarios do not cover (read models other than Inbox and Activity, search, drafts, reminders, durability across restart) is not covered by this guarantee. Format and how to add a scenario: [development guidance](development.md#contract-scenarios). Browser tests and preview use the fake client; they cannot establish native SQLite, OAuth, OS keychain, system dialogs, or WKWebView behavior. The boundary and runtime checks are recorded in [development guidance](development.md) and [current status](current-status.md).
73	
74	## Validation task boundaries
75	
76	The `mise run check` task serially runs headless core tests, the generated IPC contract check, core formatting and clippy, frontend tests, and frontend typechecking. It does not require GTK/WebKit development packages. Native shell clippy, bridge tests, and the web production build are separate tasks; `mise run check:all` runs the full sequence, including `lint:native`, serially after native prerequisites are installed. CI installs Linux prerequisites before running this full gate. Rendered Chromium suites remain opt-in and are not part of CI.
77	
78	## Implemented feature seams
79	
80	| Area | Current ownership and behavior | Contract |
81	|---|---|---|
82	| Search | Rust parses and evaluates bounded cached search in [search.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/search.rs); Gmail search and provider coverage handling are in [gmail/sync.rs](../crates/mail-core/src/gmail/sync.rs). Frontend query state and presentation are in [search.ts](../src/lib/search.ts) and `App.vue`. | [UX-07](ux-07-historical-search.md) |

91	
92	## Design proposals and limits
93	
94	The source tree does not make every proposal in [ARCHITECTURE.md](../ARCHITECTURE.md) current behavior. In particular, do not infer full multi-account/provider support, provider-synced drafts, fully quit background sync, arbitrary provider search coverage, or live macOS runtime validation from the existence of interfaces or tests. [ADR 0001](adr/0001-single-account-desktop-email-client.md), the slice contracts, feature contracts, and [current status](current-status.md) define scope and validation. New architecture recommendations belong in an explicitly labeled proposal or ADR, separate from this source inventory.

# Design System: Email OS

## 1. Overview

**Creative North Star: "The Quiet Instrument"**

A precision tool used in long, focused sessions. The surface is a single warm charcoal plane. The interface recedes until only the list, the open conversation and the next decision are on screen. Density is high but calm: 36px rows, small type, no dividers, no cards. One violet signal marks where you are. Everything else is a tonal step on the same warm gray ramp.

The system follows Superhuman's browsing look closely, and that parity is an explicit goal. It covers geometry, density, type scale, tonal layering and the focused-row treatment. Features and workflows stay our own. The one place we deliberately go our own way is state: pending, failed, partial and outcome-unknown states are always visible in their own form (*"Honest state over smooth feel"*, PRODUCT.md). A quiet surface must never hide what happened.

The system rejects Gmail-web clutter, "AI magic" sparkle chrome, generic SaaS dashboards (card grids, gradient heroes, oversized rounded panels), and optimistic UI that says "Done" before the provider confirms.

**Key Characteristics:**
- Three fixed panes: a 40px icon rail, a fluid list or reader, and a 272px darker contact pane. Each is separated by a single 1px divider.
- One content inset (50px from the list pane's left edge, 24px at the right end: `--content-inset`, `--content-inset-end`). It aligns split tabs, sender names, date-group captions, notices, banners and the bottom dock, and it carries into the reader: the subject, message senders, bodies and notes start on that x, and a docked composer's left edge sits on it.
- 36px rows on 12px type. Hierarchy comes from weight and tone, not size.
- Pane-edge alignment: the contact name sits on the split-tab line, and the contact email sits on the first-row line.
- Flat tonal layering. No shadows in the browsing shell.
- The violet accent appears once per screen: on the focused row or the active message.

**Layout geometry (approximate calibration targets).** These values come from the 2026-11-07 Superhuman reference capture (1603×2000 image px). The capture was scaled by about 1.56 image px per CSS px, calibrated from the macOS traffic-light pitch of 20pt and cross-checked against the 36px rhythm and the 40px and 270px pane widths in `superhuman-email-browsing-ux-spec.md`. Verify them on real displays.
- **Rail:** 40px wide. The top action button (28px circle) is centered on the split-tab line (42px down). The navigation icons sit in a dark pill about 30px wide that starts near the header's bottom edge, with its first glyph centered on the first list line (96px down) and a 28px pitch. The active glyph sits on a 24px Rail Pebble disc inside the pill.
- **Split header:** 78px from the content top to the first row. Tabs are vertically centered about 42px down. The hamburger is centered 23px into the pane. Tabs start at the 50px content inset with an 18px gap; the count sits 4px after its label. Compose and search icons are right-aligned on the 32px action pitch.
- **Rows:** 36px. The highlight is inset 6px from both pane edges. There is a 44px left gutter, with the 5px unread dot centered about 34px into the row. The sender column is 132px, and subject→snippet→meta gaps are 12px. The trailing date sits about 25px from the pane edge. On focus, three 16px action glyphs replace the date at a 32px pitch.
- **Date groups:** a 48px block, with the caption vertically centered on the content inset.
- **Reader:** the pane has no side padding. The reader's scroller carries the content inset (`padding-inline: 50px 24px`), so the subject, meta row, notes, loading identity and skeleton start at 50px, the same x as the list's sender text. The message stack keeps the list's focus-fill idea: each `.message` fill (the active one is Lifted Charcoal plus a 3px Dusk Lavender inset bar) spans from 6px to 6px of the pane edges, while its text stays on the inset (negative inline margin on `.messages`, inline padding on `.message`). Right edge decision: the right inset is 24px, the same as the dock, notices and composer, and the line measure is capped by `max-width: 65ch` on prose and `88ch` on monospace bodies, not by the container, so a wide pane stays left-aligned on the grid. The active message's toggle has two cues that mean different things: the 3px lavender bar says "this is the active message", and a 2px Paper White ring at a 1px offset, only on `:focus-visible`, says "the keyboard is here" (every other control keeps the lavender ring; the One Signal Rule holds because lavender still appears once). Measured at 1280×800: toggle outline `solid 2px rgb(255,255,255)` offset 1px, ring left edge at x=87 inside the message fill (46). The collapsed sender, the expanded body, the signature, `Details` and the `Show quoted text` label share one x (the message toggle and the `Details` summary carry no inline padding; the quote button pulls its 8px ghost padding into the gap with a `-8px` margin, like the selection actions: on a replica with the real class the label is at x=90 like the body, the button box at 82; before, the label was at 98). The selection-scope note and the in-pane recovery banner use the same 50px/24px. A docked composer (the reply composer and the docked new-message card) uses the undocked card's margins: `6px 24px 12px 50px`. The loading skeleton rows have the real collapsed-message pitch (1px border, 1rem padding, `--message-row-height` of 2 × Body, 0.5rem margin; about 49px at a 16px root) and start where the first message will, so the pane does not jump when the conversation arrives: the sender, date and `Loading conversation…` are ONE line (`role="status"` on the status span only); where the loaded reader has a meta row (read controls, read-only, a selection scope) that line IS the meta row's slot, and otherwise it is drawn out of flow over the first placeholder row (`.is-overlay`), which therefore paints no bar of its own. Without a list-row identity the subject slot is a hidden `h2.reader-subject` with a bar inside, so its margins match the real subject by construction. Measured in a browser with a deliberately delayed `getConversation` (fixture, no read controls, 1280×800): before, the first skeleton row was at y=244.3 and the first real message at y=187.9 (+56.4px); after, rows [187.9, 236.9, 285.9] against messages [187.9, 236.9, 285.9] (0.0px), also 0.0px at 1000×700 with a 20px root font (rows 213.2/274.2/335.2) and, as a replica with the meta-row classes and a real-shaped `.reader-meta-row`, 204.1 against 204.1. The rest of these numbers come from the CSS and are asserted by `tests/reader/geometry.test.ts`.
- **Contact pane:** 272px with a 24px inner inset. The name is centered on the tab line (42px), the email on the first list line (96px), the "Mail" label about 36px lower (~131px) and the first thread at ~156px, then a 24px pitch. Superhuman's footer toolbar sits 24px from the bottom: a ghost label plus 16px glyphs at a 28px pitch.

content.content:
194:- **Reader:** the pane has no side padding. The reader's scroller carries the content inset (`padding-inline: 50px 24px`), so the subject, meta row, notes, loading identity and skeleton start at 50px, the same x as the list's sender text. The message stack keeps the list's focus-fill idea: each `.message` fill (the active one is Lifted Charcoal plus a 3px Dusk Lavender inset bar) spans from 6px to 6px of the pane edges, while its text stays on the inset (negative inline margin on `.messages`, inline padding on `.message`). Right edge decision: the right inset is 24px, the same as the dock, notices and composer, and the line measure is capped by `max-width: 65ch` on prose and `88ch` on monospace bodies, not by the container, so a wide pane stays left-aligned on the grid. The active message's toggle has two cues that mean different things: the 3px lavender bar says "this is the active message", and a 2px Paper White ring at a 1px offset, only on `:focus-visible`, says "the keyboard is here" (every other control keeps the lavender ring; the One Signal Rule holds because lavender still appears once). Measured at 1280×800: toggle outline `solid 2px rgb(255,255,255)` offset 1px, ring left edge at x=87 inside the message fill (46). The collapsed sender, the expanded body, the signature, `Details` and the `Show quoted text` label share one x (the message toggle and the `Details` summary carry no inline padding; the quote button pulls its 8px ghost padding into the gap with a `-8px` margin, like the selection actions: on a replica with the real class the label is at x=90 like the body, the button box at 82; before, the label was at 98). The selection-scope note and the in-pane recovery banner use the same 50px/24px. A docked composer (the reply composer and the docked new-message card) uses the undocked card's margins: `6px 24px 12px 50px`. The loading skeleton rows have the real collapsed-message pitch (1px border, 1rem padding, `--message-row-height` of 2 × Body, 0.5rem margin; about 49px at a 16px root) and start where the first message will, so the pane does not jump when the conversation arrives: the sender, date and `Loading conversation…` are ONE line (`role="status"` on the status span only); where the loaded reader has a meta row (read controls, read-only, a selection scope) that line IS the meta row's slot, and otherwise it is drawn out of flow over the first placeholder row (`.is-overlay`), which therefore paints no bar of its own. Without a list-row identity the subject slot is a hidden `h2.reader-subject` with a bar inside, so its margins match the real subject by construction. Measured in a browser with a deliberately delayed `getConversation` (fixture, no read controls, 1280×800): before, the first skeleton row was at y=244.3 and the first real message at y=187.9 (+56.4px); after, rows [187.9, 236.9, 285.9] against messages [187.9, 236.9, 285.9] (0.0px), also 0.0px at 1000×700 with a 20px root font (rows 213.2/274.2/335.2) and, as a replica with the meta-row classes and a real-shaped `.reader-meta-row`, 204.1 against 204.1. The rest of these numbers come from the CSS and are asserted by `tests/reader/geometry.test.ts`.
207:2. **Rail.** Done (2026-11-07 rail/contact layout pass). The rail is a fixed 40px column (px, so larger root fonts widen the list, never the rail) with a 1px Seam on its right.
220:7. **Row actions.** Done (rows pass): `icon-muted` inline SVG glyphs (`RowGlyph.vue`) replace the date on the focused or hovered row only. Accessible names, roving tab stops and the `meta-compact` disclosure stay. The disclosure now also re-measures on text-size changes inside an unchanged row box (rail/contact pass: the sender label is observed too). Remaining: Superhuman shows done/snooze/more; we show only our real actions (read/unread, done).
229:   - **No rows, no column (gap 18):** while a ready list has no rows, no reader is open and no reply target exists, there is no conversation to have a contact: the column is not rendered and its grid track goes (`.app-main.contact-collapsed`), so the list takes the width instead of leaving a blank 272px slab; below 1000px the rail's Contact button is absent, so it cannot open an empty drawer. A loading or failed list does not collapse (rows may still arrive); with rows, nothing changes. If focus was inside the contact surface when the last row went, it moves to the empty line.
232:10. **Palette deltas.** Done: `text-primary` #ece9e2 → #ffffff (typeset pass), `text-secondary` #a8a29a → #c0bcb6 (rows pass), `text-tertiary`, `icon-muted` and `unread-marker` added (header and rows passes), the undefined `--text-muted` on coverage notes now maps to `text-secondary`, and `rail-well` / `rail-button` are CSS tokens (rail pass). `divider` is now #474543 (polish pass): the rail and contact-pane seams, the drawer's leading edge, utility-chip and input borders, the compact row-actions popover and the command-overlay hint rule. It never separates rows (the list has no row borders). The old #3b3936 survives as the quieter `rule` token for structure inside a pane, only in the reader (toolbar and message rules), the composer's own structure and the Account panel, so those surfaces keep their tone until a reader reference is captured. Drawer rows and the Activity group detail no longer use it (gap 20), and neither do the Reminders rows and picker (gap 21). `focus-accent` stays at the committed #bba5ed; the capture reads about #bfa1f6, which is within capture and color-profile noise.
233:11. **Global button style.** Done (polish pass). The `button` defaults are zero-specificity (`:where()`), so every component class keeps its own look. The default is a ghost: transparent, Paper White, 4px radius, `4px 8px` (24px tall at 12px, the old chip's hit target), Lifted Charcoal on hover, Focus Stone on press, 0.45 opacity when disabled, and the 2px Dusk Lavender focus ring at a 1px offset. The selection bar, the action notice's Undo, Load more, the search form and the reader toolbar are ghost text buttons. Bordered `button-utility` chips (Lifted Charcoal, 1px Seam, `3px 8px`) appear only inside utility drawers, the modal attachment chooser, recovery banners (`.recovery-banner`: draft-close recovery, inbox/account load errors, the reader's navigation error, the header's saved-split error) and the synthetic workspace strip. Fields follow "Inputs / Fields": a Seam border that shifts to Dusk Lavender (plus a 1px inner outline) on keyboard focus, Smoke placeholders (4.76:1 on Lifted Charcoal) and a lavender ring on native checkboxes.
234:12. **Command overlay.** Done (polish pass; structure pass: groups, per-command glyphs, aliases, Keys list, "no match" copy, caption removed). The off-palette values the overlay still carried (#56534e border and rules, #c9c4bc caption, icon and hint text, #d4cfc7 disabled reasons, #66615b `kbd` fill, `.85rem` radius, the 46rem width, 24px query and 1.5rem glyph) are now tokens: a 576px Lifted Charcoal panel with a 10px radius, no border, Overlay lift over a `rgba(0,0,0,0.53)` backdrop at 15vh. The query is 16px on Deep Umber with a 1px Dusk Lavender border, items are 36px rows of 12px Body with 16px Graphite glyphs, the highlighted item is Focus Stone plus a 3px Dusk Lavender bar, disabled items are Smoke with Ash reasons, and `kbd` is Ash on Deep Umber. Geometry is whole-pixel so a highlighted item scrolled into view is never clipped. The modal attachment chooser shares the panel (46rem wide, 12px body), which closes the "chooser body inherits 16px" remainder of gap 14. (The violets this gap once listed were already gone before this pass.)
236:14. **Type scale and dates.** Done (2026-11-07 typeset pass). The shell type is semantic tokens on `:root`: `--type-headline` 1rem, `--type-body` 0.75rem, `--type-count` 0.6875rem, `--type-mono` 0.85rem, weights 400/600 only (`--weight-regular`, `--weight-strong`). `.app-main` sets Body as the shell default, so the rail, contact pane, notices, drawers, the reader chrome and form controls are 12px instead of an inherited 16px or ad hoc 0.8/0.85/0.9/0.95/1.1rem. Shell h2 is Headline; h3/h4 and in-panel drawer headings are Title; the reader subject is Headline at 600. Row dates follow the Label rules below and are deterministic (no default-locale dependence: the old `30 Sept 2001` vs `Sep 30, 2001` rendered-layout gate now passes under any `LANG`). Rows carry `<time datetime>` plus the full date as the title; reader message times are full dates with `datetime`. The rendered larger-text gate expected the compact action disclosure at a 25px root font (was 23px) after this pass, and at 34.5px (expanded at 30px) after the rail/contact pass, since the fixed-px rail and contact pane leave the list wider at every text size.
237:   Polish pass: the remaining raw timestamps (Account "Last synced", Cached Done coverage "Last synced", Activity group times, Provider mail catalog, page, recovery-snapshot and message times, Reminders due times, the reader's recovery snapshot) now go through `FullDate.vue`, which renders `fullDateLabel` in a `<time datetime>`. The command overlay and the attachment chooser are on the scale (gaps 12 and 14). Remaining (closed by gap 20): the Reminders time input took a typed ISO value; the typed field now sits behind a `Custom` toggle and preset times fill the same value.
247:   - **Inline attachments and human sizes.** An expanded message with `hasAttachment === true` lists its files under the body: a plain list, no cards, one 24px line per file (16px Ash paperclip, filename in Paper White with an ellipsis and the full name as its title, then `27 B · text/plain` in Ash, then a ghost `Save` with the accessible name `Save <file name>`). While a file transfers, its `Save` button stays mounted, `aria-disabled` and reads `Saving…` (accessible name `Saving <file name>`), with a `Cancel` beside it, so keyboard focus never falls to the page (the same idea as Retry; when `Cancel` held focus and the transfer stops, `Save` takes it back; focus that moved elsewhere is left alone; no live region is added); success is an Ash `role="status"` line (`Saved to Downloads as <name>. No file was opened.`, or the modelled preview wording), failure is a Coral Fault `role="alert"` line with the chooser's wording. Files over 5 MB show `Over the 5 MB limit; cannot download.` and no button. A retained snapshot disables Save with a title. A message that claims files with no cached descriptor says `Attachment details are not cached. Sync to fetch.`; `false` or unknown claims show nothing. Descriptors load once per conversation after the snapshot renders and are kept for the reader session; a failed load (`Could not load file details.`) offers a ghost `Retry` that asks again (see Reader Message Disclosures). Sizes are binary steps with mail-client names (`27 B`, `1.0 KB`, `4.6 MB`; `unknown size` for a non-number). Names are printed with bidirectional control characters (U+202A–202E, U+2066–2069, U+200E/F, U+061C) removed, so `invoice\u202Efdp.exe` reads in its real order; the same applies to the chooser and the saved-as line. A size that one decimal would round across the limit prints exact bytes (`5,242,881 B` next to `Over the 5 MB limit`, never `5.0 MB`). The Cmd+O chooser keeps links and the full list and uses the same transfer logic (`useAttachmentTransfer`) but its own instance: a transfer started inline is not shown in the chooser, and closing the chooser cancels only its own transfer. Its file buttons read `Save` too (and also stay mounted as `aria-disabled` `Saving…` while a transfer runs, as does `Reload file list`, so its Escape and Tab trap keep hearing keys; focus leaves `Cancel transfer` for the file's `Save` when it goes away), with the accessible name `Save <file name>` (they used to read `Save to Downloads`; only the success line names Downloads). Its intro shrinks to `Download only.
