213:   - **Activity badge:** a small Amber Notice count on the Activity glyph shows unresolved operations, i.e. `queued`/`applying` plus `outcome_unknown`. It is derived from the activity rows the drawer already lists, with no new read. The digit is `aria-hidden`; the words ("2 operations pending", "1 operation with outcome unknown", or "3 operations unresolved: 2 pending, 1 outcome unknown") are the button's `aria-describedby` and are appended to its title. The badge disappears at zero.
216:3. **Row metrics.** Done (2026-11-07 rows pass): 12px type in two weights, a fixed 36px height, no per-row dividers, the 6px pane inset, the 44px left gutter and the 132px sender column. Leading caption: done (polish pass). When the list opens with Today, that caption is visually hidden (it stays in the accessibility tree), so the first row is centered on the 96px first-list line with the rail's first glyph and the contact email, as in the reference. Today's rows already show a time, so nothing is lost on screen. Any other leading bucket (Yesterday, Earlier this month, a month, Unknown date) stays visible, because a list that starts in the past must say where it starts; in that case the first row is still centered 144px down.
220:7. **Row actions.** Done (rows pass): `icon-muted` inline SVG glyphs (`RowGlyph.vue`) replace the date on the focused or hovered row only. The disclosure now also re-measures on text-size changes inside an unchanged row box (rail/contact pass: the sender label is observed too). Remaining: Superhuman shows done/snooze/more; we show only our real actions (read/unread, done).
226:   - **Copy controls:** each copy control is a 16px Graphite glyph in the trailing slot of its own line, revealed by opacity on line hover or focus. It stays focusable, and it no longer leaves an empty line when hidden. Without a display name, Copy email moves to the name line.
227:   - **Recent cached mail:** a Title label with a 16px envelope glyph (~129px), then plain Ash text rows at a 24px pitch (first at 156px). Each row has an ellipsis and the full subject as its title, rises to Paper White on hover or focus, and is still a button.

The query is 16px on Deep Umber with a 1px Dusk Lavender border, items are 36px rows of 12px Body with 16px Graphite glyphs, the highlighted item is Focus Stone plus a 3px Dusk Lavender bar, disabled items are Smoke with Ash reasons, and `kbd` is Ash on Deep Umber. Geometry is whole-pixel so a highlighted item scrolled into view is never clipped. The modal attachment chooser shares the panel (46rem wide, 12px body), which closes the "chooser body inherits 16px" remainder of gap 14. (The violets this gap once listed were already gone before this pass.)
236:14. **Type scale and dates.** Done (2026-11-07 typeset pass). The shell type is semantic tokens on `:root`: `--type-headline` 1rem, `--type-body` 0.75rem, `--type-count` 0.6875rem, `--type-mono` 0.85rem, weights 400/600 only (`--weight-regular`, `--weight-strong`). `.app-main` sets Body as the shell default, so the rail, contact pane, notices, drawers, the reader chrome and form controls are 12px instead of an inherited 16px or ad hoc 0.8/0.85/0.9/0.95/1.1rem. Shell h2 is Headline; h3/h4 and in-panel drawer headings are Title; the reader subject is Headline at 600. Row dates follow the Label rules below and are deterministic (no default-locale dependence: the old `30 Sept 2001` vs `Sep 30, 2001` rendered-layout gate now passes under any `LANG`). Rows carry `<time datetime>` plus the full date as the title; reader message times are full dates with `datetime`. The rendered larger-text gate expected the compact action disclosure at a 25px root font (was 23px) after this pass, and at 34.5px (expanded at 30px) after the rail/contact pass, since the fixed-px rail and contact pane leave the list wider at every text size.
238:15. **Typeface.** Superhuman ships a proprietary face. We stay on local `system-ui` (no remote fonts), so glyph widths will differ slightly. Calibrate sizes by eye on device, not by matching the font.
242:   - **Status line and caveats (follow-up).** The status line stays terse (`Saved locally · not sent`). The caveats (recipients stored as typed and not validated; no Bcc, reply-all or rich text) are one extra Ash line behind a small info button next to it (`aria-expanded`, 14px Ash glyph, `About local drafts`), so keyboard users reach them; the `title` is a bonus, not the only route. The status line is no longer a live region: a separate visually hidden `role="status"` region announces only the first settled state, a problem (`Save not confirmed`, `Conflict — edits preserved`) and the recovery after one, never the `Saving…`/`Saved` autosave cycle. Error lines keep `role="alert"`. A successful discard closes the editor and says nothing of its own (the confirm dialog is the announcement).
248:   - **R and contrast.** `R` prepares a reply from the open reader, from the same rule as the buttons (ready, not Cached Trash, not blocked by an incomplete conversation, a retained snapshot or mismatched headers, no drawer or composer open). The source is always the displayed latest message, never the focused one. The reply body takes focus from anything that is not a text field (`<body>`, the reply button, the reader article after a click on message text, a `Details` summary, a participant), never from a text field the user moved to. After Discard focus returns to the reader's active message. It is inert in text fields, during IME composition, with modifiers, on key repeat and from other buttons. "Reply" appears in the palette with `R` only while it can run, and the reply controls' titles read `Reply — R` (the accessible name of the toolbar button is `Reply`; the per-message glyph, which does the same thing, is `Reply to latest message` so a screen reader can tell the two apart, and both keep the `Reply — R` title). The blocked-reply notices, `Cancel reply preparation` and the `reply_unavailable` draft error keep the word "preparation". Closing the composer returns focus to the reader's active message. Graphite is 2.75:1 on Focus Stone and 3.79:1 on Lifted Charcoal, so it is never used for meaningful glyphs or text on a focus fill or on the composer fill; new hints and glyphs use Ash (4.99:1 and 6.86:1). The reader's `Details` summary moved from Graphite to Ash for that reason; the reply glyph on the active message stays Graphite at rest (3.79:1 clears the 3:1 glyph floor) and rises to Paper White on hover and focus.
252:   - **Affordances:** a Graphite composer field boundary (documented exception), a 24px caveat target, a focus ring and role on participants, `Save` with per-file names in the chooser, `Retry` for file details, alt text on the Details glyph, and the pending line is the reader's one `role="status"`.
254:   - **Kept as is:** the subject (16px, 600) over the body (15px, 400) separates by weight, position and the sender row between them; changing the size would break the Headline role and the Two-Size Rule, and nothing can be measured without a render. If a render shows the subject blending in, try tone before size.
259:   - **Glyphs and names:** Reminders is a bell, Remind me is the clock; the per-message reply glyph is `Reply to latest message`.
271:   - **Cached Trash.** A browse context (`'trash'`) beside Done and Starred, served by `listCachedTrash` through the same paged, replayable, per-request-fenced list read (100 rows a page, `Load more Cached Trash`). It renders the shared `InboxList` rows (sender, subject, snippet, compact date, attachment glyph, 36px) in a read-only mode: no checkbox or selection mode, no action glyphs or disclosure, no read toggles, and Cmd/Shift-click only opens. Rows still focus (J/K, arrows) and open (Enter, click). It is not a mutation surface: `E`, `Shift+E`, `Z`, `U`, `S`, `H`, `X`, bulk selection, `R` and every palette mutation stay unavailable in the list and in its reader, and the Action notice is hidden there. `C` (compose) behaves as in Done.
276:   - **Reminders (phase 2).** A list context (`'reminders'`, offered whenever the client has a reminders transport: fixture and Gmail, `remindersSupported`) beside Done and Trash, entered from the header glyph (`Reminders (G then H)`, `aria-current="page"` and Paper White while the list is showing), `G H`, the palette and the navigator, and from `H` (`Remind me`) on an Inbox row or an open reader. There is no new rail slot and no new backend call: the rows are `client.reminders.list()` plus the live change subscription, read through `useReminders` (which holds every request rule of the old drawer: per-request staleness, exact retry of a lost ACK, the validation message for `dueAt`, the newer-message preparation error). The context is pushed on the history stack, so Back and Escape return to the prior context and row, and a reader opened from a reminder returns to the same reminder row (J/K do not walk between reminders).
283:   - **Drafts (phase 3).** A list context (`'drafts'`, any account) beside Done, Trash and Reminders. Entries are unchanged: the rail item (`rail-drafts`, a plain navigation item with `aria-current="page"` while the list is showing and no reader or editor covers it, never `aria-expanded`) and the palette action `Go to local Drafts`. The context h1 is `Drafts`, shown styled like an active tab; the previous context is pushed on the history stack, so Back and Escape return to it. Draft rows are not threads, so they use `ContextRowList` through `DraftsList`: the recipient (Title, Paper White; Ash `(no recipient)`) is the open button, the subject follows (Body; Ash `(no subject)`), and the trailing slot holds a quiet Ash `Reply` word for reply drafts, the `Conflict · revision N` word (Amber Notice, only on the draft in conflict) and the compact updated time with its full date as the title. The revision is a row title. One Ash coverage line sits on the 50px inset (`data-test="drafts-coverage"`, `role="note"`): `Local to this device · never sent`, the sentence in its title and hidden text, with a quiet `New draft` ghost on its trailing side that does what `C` and the header compose glyph do. Empty text: `No local drafts.` Every recovery and error line (suspended editor of another account, close error, close-protection setup and retry, list error, subscription error and retry, open error) is in flow above the rows with unchanged wording and hooks; an open error never hides the rows. While an editor covers the list, the app shows the list and subscription lines in the list notices and the close-protection banner as before.
287:   - **Keys.** The list uses the Context Row model (J/K, arrows, Home, End; `G` chords and Left still work from a row). Mailbox shortcuts (`E`, `Z`, `U`, `S`, `H`, `X`, `R`, selection) are inert in the list. `C` and the header glyph open a new-message card from it.
313:   - **One account status note in the header.** In the same slot and pattern as the preview tag and the read-only hint (`.header-note`, one line, gives up width before the glyphs, optional `.header-link`): `Not connected`, `Sign-in expired`, `Finish sign-in in your browser`, `Gmail not configured`, `Syncing…` (`Syncing first mail · N cached` during the first sync) and `Sync failed` with the cause in words when it is known: `Sync failed · no network` (a `network_unavailable` sync error; there is no "Offline" wording anywhere: offline is not a core state, only a `network_unavailable` sync error, and the user chose the failure-first wording), `Sync failed · rate limited`, `Sync failed · provider unavailable`, `Sync failed · storage unavailable`. Other or missing causes say plain `Sync failed`, so an unknown cause is never relabelled. The cause is visible words, not only a `title`. The first sync keeps its count after the cause (`Sync failed · no network · 0 cached`). **Count wording, one form per kind of place:** a standalone fact says `N conversations cached` (`1 conversation cached`), and the Account drawer says it in every state, including the first sync; the compact first-sync line, the header note (`Syncing first mail · N cached`, `Sync failed · no network · N cached`) and its twin in the empty line (`Syncing first mail… N cached.`), keeps the short `N cached` because the header has no room for the long form and the two surfaces must say the same words. The note's action link (`Connect Gmail`, `Sign in again`, `Cancel sign-in`, `Retry`) is shown **only when the empty inbox line is not already carrying the action** (one action, one place); a not-configured device has a single `Account` link, in the empty line or, when that line is not showing, in the header. **One name per action on every surface** (empty line, header link, palette, Account drawer, Provider mail note): `Connect Gmail` (disconnected only: a device that is not configured has nothing to connect with, so there is no Connect button, palette command or Provider mail link there, only `Account` and the next step), `Sign in again` (expired sign-in), `Cancel sign-in`, `Retry`, `Sync now`. **Empty-line ownership:** while the empty line shows (zero rows, plain Inbox, no reader) and says a status (every kind except the plain connected-and-synced empty text), the header note drops its visible words, link and chip, so the header shows only the Preview tag; the `account-status-note` element stays as a visually hidden `role=status` carrying the one announcement (the empty line is not a live region), so nothing is read twice and the ticking cached count is shown once, in the empty line. When rows exist, or the empty line only reports an empty inbox (a later `Syncing…` stays), the note shows as before. **No double announcement, no duplicate Retry:** while the Account drawer is open and shows the same typed sync failure as its `role=alert` (with its own Retry), the header note loses its `role=status`, hides its hidden text from assistive technology and drops its visible words and link (`drawerShowsSameFailure`); the Preview tag stays. The note returns with its words, link and announcement when the drawer closes (the empty line behind the drawer drops its own `Retry` for the same reason). A failure with no typed cause has no drawer alert, and connection notes are not repeated by it, so neither is hidden. Connection notes are not repeated by the drawer's alert, so they keep announcing. A neutral note's lead may ellipsize; the lead of a failure or an expired sign-in and the link never do, and the cause detail is whole or hidden with its dot (see the closing pass below). The detail is the note's `title` and visually hidden text and never contains the ticking cached count, so it is announced once. Nothing shows while connected and idle or in fixture mode. **Any status note, connection or sync, replaces the read-only hint** (the Account drawer covers it; the header has no room for both). The note never says actions are off: actions depend on `mutationAccess`, not on the connection, so the only standing fact it states is that cached mail stays readable. Tones: a sync failure is Coral Fault (a confirmed failure, with words), Sign-in expired is Amber Notice, the rest is Ash.
314:   - **Header width rule (follow-up to the 1030px critique).** At the 1030px floor the preview tag, the account note, the read-only hint and the `Unread only` chip used to crush the active tab to 4px (measured x=90, w=4 on the old grid). Second pass: the header grid's tab column is `minmax(min(var(--header-tabs-floor), 100%), 1fr)` with a fixed `--header-tabs-floor: 10rem` (about `Inbox 18`, the 18px gap and the `Unread only` chip), so the tab strip never drops below it; the trail column takes what is left. Third pass (the 1030px critique with a saved split, `Unread only` and the read-only hint still left `Inbox` 13px wide with no label): the floor is built from what is really in the strip, `--header-tabs-floor: max(10rem, Inbox + saved tab + chips)` with `--tab-inbox: 4.5rem` (`Inbox 18` measured 62px), `--tab-saved: 9rem` (a saved label stops at `12ch` with an ellipsis, its full name is the tab's `title`, plus the count) and `--header-chip: 4.75rem` (`Unread only` measured 73px), plus the 18px gaps, added by `:has()` rules on the header for a second tab and for each chip. Tabs and the nav are `flex: 0 0 auto`: a tab never shrinks, so a note can never take a tab's label. At 1100px and below the read-only hint collapses to its `Review access` link (the words become visually hidden, so they stay in the accessibility tree and the hover title) and the link never clips, so the hint gives up width before anything else. Estimated at 1030px (list column 718px): tabs 328px, glyphs about 190px, collapsed hint about 90px; with the browser-preview Preview tag as well (never in the native app) the hint ellipsizes first. Inside the trail the glyphs are `flex: 0 0 auto` and never shrink; the notes shrink in this order: Preview tag (`flex-shrink: 4`, but never below 5.5rem), read-only hint (`2`), account status note (`1`, link fixed). Measured in a real browser at 1030px with the worst case (first sync failed, preview, chip): tabs 160px, `Inbox 18` 62px, chip 73px, preview 96px, status 244px, glyphs unmoved; the same content on the old grid gave tabs 4px. jsdom cannot lay anything out, so the tests pin the CSS rules (the floor variables and `:has()` rules, non-shrinking tabs, the `12ch` cap, the 1100px hint collapse) and the hint, ownership and action logic (`readOnlyHintShown`, `emptyLineOwnsStatus`, `headerNoteAnnounces`, `headerNoticeAction`), not the pixels. The third-pass floor was computed from the measured widths above and the tokens, not re-measured in a browser (none was available).

Without a list-row identity the subject slot is a hidden `h2.reader-subject` with a bar inside, so its margins match the real subject by construction. Measured in a browser with a deliberately delayed `getConversation` (fixture, no read controls, 1280×800): before, the first skeleton row was at y=244.3 and the first real message at y=187.9 (+56.4px); after, rows [187.9, 236.9, 285.9] against messages [187.9, 236.9, 285.9] (0.0px), also 0.0px at 1000×700 with a 20px root font (rows 213.2/274.2/335.2) and, as a replica with the meta-row classes and a real-shaped `.reader-meta-row`, 204.1 against 204.1. The rest of these numbers come from the CSS and are asserted by `tests/reader/geometry.test.ts`.
195:- **Contact pane:** 272px with a 24px inner inset. The name is centered on the tab line (42px), the email on the first list line (96px), the "Mail" label about 36px lower (~131px) and the first thread at ~156px, then a 24px pitch. Superhuman's footer toolbar sits 24px from the bottom: a ghost label plus 16px glyphs at a 28px pitch.
201:1. **Split header.** Done (2026-11-07 header pass). The header is one borderless 78px strip inside the list column (the rail and contact pane span its height). It has a Graphite hamburger (Destinations navigator) centered 23px in, split tabs on the 50px inset (16px, active Paper White, inactive Smoke, 11px Ash count 4px after the label, 18px apart), and right-hand glyphs on the 32px pitch: Back (when there is history), Reminders (a bell, while the reader's `Remind me on this device` action and the row action keep the clock, so the view and the action never share a glyph), the Starred-only toggle, Commands and Search. There is no brand text, no visible h1 while a tab is active, and no bordered chips. Glyphs are local inline SVG (`HeaderGlyph.vue`).
205:   - Utility drawers now start below the header, so they never cover its glyphs.
206:   Update: the compose glyph now ships. It sits on the right of the header, left of Search, as a Graphite glyph on the 32px pitch, and opens the local-draft compose card INLINE in the central pane ("New Message", C key / palette action "Compose new local draft") — an in-flow card that replaces the list while composing, not a modal overlay: no backdrop and no dimming, so the rail, header and contact pane stay visible. (While a reader is open, the card docks at the bottom of the reader pane, like the reply composer.) There is still no compose capability beyond local drafts, so the glyph opens the local-only inline card, never a sender. (The aggregate pending count now lives on the Activity rail badge, and the tab line is calibrated against the rail's home circle: both are centered 42px down; see gap 2.)
209:   - **Inkwell pill:** a 30px pill (the capture measures ~30px, not 28px) holds Starred (Gmail), Cached Done, Provider mail and Cached Trash (Gmail) as 16px glyphs on 28px hit targets at a 28px pitch. Its first glyph is centered on the first list line.
210:   - **Utilities:** Account (Gmail), Activity, Drafts and the narrow-viewport Contact disclosure are ghost glyphs at the bottom, 16px from the edge. Account and Activity open drawers; Drafts is a navigation item (a list context, gap 21) and carries `aria-current` while its list is showing.
211:   - **States:** the current destination (`aria-current`) or open drawer (`aria-expanded`) shows a Paper White glyph on a 24px Rail Pebble disc; the rest are Graphite and rise to Paper White on hover and focus.
212:   - **Labels:** every button keeps its text label as its accessible name (a visually hidden span, so `textContent` is unchanged), its hover `title` (the action label with its shortcut, as on the header glyphs), and a keyboard tooltip: the same label shown beside the rail on `:focus-visible`, with Popover lift.
213:   - **Activity badge:** a small Amber Notice count on the Activity glyph shows unresolved operations, i.e. `queued`/`applying` plus `outcome_unknown`. It is derived from the activity rows the drawer already lists, with no new read. The digit is `aria-hidden`; the words ("2 operations pending", "1 operation with outcome unknown", or "3 operations unresolved: 2 pending, 1 outcome unknown") are the button's `aria-describedby` and are appended to its title. The badge disappears at zero.
216:3. **Row metrics.** Done (2026-11-07 rows pass): 12px type in two weights, a fixed 36px height, no per-row dividers, the 6px pane inset, the 44px left gutter and the 132px sender column. Leading caption: done (polish pass). When the list opens with Today, that caption is visually hidden (it stays in the accessibility tree), so the first row is centered on the 96px first-list line with the rail's first glyph and the contact email, as in the reference. Today's rows already show a time, so nothing is lost on screen. Any other leading bucket (Yesterday, Earlier this month, a month, Unknown date) stays visible, because a list that starts in the past must say where it starts; in that case the first row is still centered 144px down.
220:7. **Row actions.** Done (rows pass): `icon-muted` inline SVG glyphs (`RowGlyph.vue`) replace the date on the focused or hovered row only. Accessible names, roving tab stops and the `meta-compact` disclosure stay. The disclosure now also re-measures on text-size changes inside an unchanged row box (rail/contact pass: the sender label is observed too). Remaining: Superhuman shows done/snooze/more; we show only our real actions (read/unread, done).
226:   - **Copy controls:** each copy control is a 16px Graphite glyph in the trailing slot of its own line, revealed by opacity on line hover or focus. It stays focusable, and it no longer leaves an empty line when hidden. Without a display name, Copy email moves to the name line.
227:   - **Recent cached mail:** a Title label with a 16px envelope glyph (~129px), then plain Ash text rows at a 24px pitch (first at 156px). Each row has an ellipsis and the full subject as its title, rises to Paper White on hover or focus, and is still a button.
234:12. **Command overlay.** Done (polish pass; structure pass: groups, per-command glyphs, aliases, Keys list, "no match" copy, caption removed). The off-palette values the overlay still carried (#56534e border and rules, #c9c4bc caption, icon and hint text, #d4cfc7 disabled reasons, #66615b `kbd` fill, `.85rem` radius, the 46rem width, 24px query and 1.5rem glyph) are now tokens: a 576px Lifted Charcoal panel with a 10px radius, no border, Overlay lift over a `rgba(0,0,0,0.53)` backdrop at 15vh. The query is 16px on Deep Umber with a 1px Dusk Lavender border, items are 36px rows of 12px Body with 16px Graphite glyphs, the highlighted item is Focus Stone plus a 3px Dusk Lavender bar, disabled items are Smoke with Ash reasons, and `kbd` is Ash on Deep Umber. Geometry is whole-pixel so a highlighted item scrolled into view is never clipped. The modal attachment chooser shares the panel (46rem wide, 12px body), which closes the "chooser body inherits 16px" remainder of gap 14. (The violets this gap once listed were already gone before this pass.)
236:14. **Type scale and dates.** Done (2026-11-07 typeset pass). The shell type is semantic tokens on `:root`: `--type-headline` 1rem, `--type-body` 0.75rem, `--type-count` 0.6875rem, `--type-mono` 0.85rem, weights 400/600 only (`--weight-regular`, `--weight-strong`). `.app-main` sets Body as the shell default, so the rail, contact pane, notices, drawers, the reader chrome and form controls are 12px instead of an inherited 16px or ad hoc 0.8/0.85/0.9/0.95/1.1rem. Shell h2 is Headline; h3/h4 and in-panel drawer headings are Title; the reader subject is Headline at 600. Row dates follow the Label rules below and are deterministic (no default-locale dependence: the old `30 Sept 2001` vs `Sep 30, 2001` rendered-layout gate now passes under any `LANG`). Rows carry `<time datetime>` plus the full date as the title; reader message times are full dates with `datetime`. The rendered larger-text gate expected the compact action disclosure at a 25px root font (was 23px) after this pass, and at 34.5px (expanded at 30px) after the rail/contact pass, since the fixed-px rail and contact pane leave the list wider at every text size.
238:15. **Typeface.** Superhuman ships a proprietary face. We stay on local `system-ui` (no remote fonts), so glyph widths will differ slightly. Calibrate sizes by eye on device, not by matching the font.
242:   - **Status line and caveats (follow-up).** The status line stays terse (`Saved locally · not sent`). The caveats (recipients stored as typed and not validated; no Bcc, reply-all or rich text) are one extra Ash line behind a small info button next to it (`aria-expanded`, 14px Ash glyph, `About local drafts`), so keyboard users reach them; the `title` is a bonus, not the only route. The status line is no longer a live region: a separate visually hidden `role="status"` region announces only the first settled state, a problem (`Save not confirmed`, `Conflict — edits preserved`) and the recovery after one, never the `Saving…`/`Saved` autosave cycle. Error lines keep `role="alert"`. A successful discard closes the editor and says nothing of its own (the confirm dialog is the announcement).
248:   - **R and contrast.** `R` prepares a reply from the open reader, from the same rule as the buttons (ready, not Cached Trash, not blocked by an incomplete conversation, a retained snapshot or mismatched headers, no drawer or composer open). The source is always the displayed latest message, never the focused one. The reply body takes focus from anything that is not a text field (`<body>`, the reply button, the reader article after a click on message text, a `Details` summary, a participant), never from a text field the user moved to. After Discard focus returns to the reader's active message. It is inert in text fields, during IME composition, with modifiers, on key repeat and from other buttons. "Reply" appears in the palette with `R` only while it can run, and the reply controls' titles read `Reply — R` (the accessible name of the toolbar button is `Reply`; the per-message glyph, which does the same thing, is `Reply to latest message` so a screen reader can tell the two apart, and both keep the `Reply — R` title). The blocked-reply notices, `Cancel reply preparation` and the `reply_unavailable` draft error keep the word "preparation". Closing the composer returns focus to the reader's active message. Graphite is 2.75:1 on Focus Stone and 3.79:1 on Lifted Charcoal, so it is never used for meaningful glyphs or text on a focus fill or on the composer fill; new hints and glyphs use Ash (4.99:1 and 6.86:1). The reader's `Details` summary moved from Graphite to Ash for that reason; the reply glyph on the active message stays Graphite at rest (3.79:1 clears the 3:1 glyph floor) and rises to Paper White on hover and focus.
252:   - **Affordances:** a Graphite composer field boundary (documented exception), a 24px caveat target, a focus ring and role on participants, `Save` with per-file names in the chooser, `Retry` for file details, alt text on the Details glyph, and the pending line is the reader's one `role="status"`.
254:   - **Kept as is:** the subject (16px, 600) over the body (15px, 400) separates by weight, position and the sender row between them; changing the size would break the Headline role and the Two-Size Rule, and nothing can be measured without a render. If a render shows the subject blending in, try tone before size.
259:   - **Glyphs and names:** Reminders is a bell, Remind me is the clock; the per-message reply glyph is `Reply to latest message`.
271:   - **Cached Trash.** A browse context (`'trash'`) beside Done and Starred, served by `listCachedTrash` through the same paged, replayable, per-request-fenced list read (100 rows a page, `Load more Cached Trash`). It renders the shared `InboxList` rows (sender, subject, snippet, compact date, attachment glyph, 36px) in a read-only mode: no checkbox or selection mode, no action glyphs or disclosure, no read toggles, and Cmd/Shift-click only opens. Rows still focus (J/K, arrows) and open (Enter, click). It is not a mutation surface: `E`, `Shift+E`, `Z`, `U`, `S`, `H`, `X`, bulk selection, `R` and every palette mutation stay unavailable in the list and in its reader, and the Action notice is hidden there. `C` (compose) behaves as in Done.
276:   - **Reminders (phase 2).** A list context (`'reminders'`, offered whenever the client has a reminders transport: fixture and Gmail, `remindersSupported`) beside Done and Trash, entered from the header glyph (`Reminders (G then H)`, `aria-current="page"` and Paper White while the list is showing), `G H`, the palette and the navigator, and from `H` (`Remind me`) on an Inbox row or an open reader. There is no new rail slot and no new backend call: the rows are `client.reminders.list()` plus the live change subscription, read through `useReminders` (which holds every request rule of the old drawer: per-request staleness, exact retry of a lost ACK, the validation message for `dueAt`, the newer-message preparation error). The context is pushed on the history stack, so Back and Escape return to the prior context and row, and a reader opened from a reminder returns to the same reminder row (J/K do not walk between reminders).
283:   - **Drafts (phase 3).** A list context (`'drafts'`, any account) beside Done, Trash and Reminders. Entries are unchanged: the rail item (`rail-drafts`, a plain navigation item with `aria-current="page"` while the list is showing and no reader or editor covers it, never `aria-expanded`) and the palette action `Go to local Drafts`. The context h1 is `Drafts`, shown styled like an active tab; the previous context is pushed on the history stack, so Back and Escape return to it. Draft rows are not threads, so they use `ContextRowList` through `DraftsList`: the recipient (Title, Paper White; Ash `(no recipient)`) is the open button, the subject follows (Body; Ash `(no subject)`), and the trailing slot holds a quiet Ash `Reply` word for reply drafts, the `Conflict · revision N` word (Amber Notice, only on the draft in conflict) and the compact updated time with its full date as the title. The revision is a row title. One Ash coverage line sits on the 50px inset (`data-test="drafts-coverage"`, `role="note"`): `Local to this device · never sent`, the sentence in its title and hidden text, with a quiet `New draft` ghost on its trailing side that does what `C` and the header compose glyph do. Empty text: `No local drafts.` Every recovery and error line (suspended editor of another account, close error, close-protection setup and retry, list error, subscription error and retry, open error) is in flow above the rows with unchanged wording and hooks; an open error never hides the rows. While an editor covers the list, the app shows the list and subscription lines in the list notices and the close-protection banner as before.
287:   - **Keys.** The list uses the Context Row model (J/K, arrows, Home, End; `G` chords and Left still work from a row). Mailbox shortcuts (`E`, `Z`, `U`, `S`, `H`, `X`, `R`, selection) are inert in the list. `C` and the header glyph open a new-message card from it.
313:   - **One account status note in the header.** In the same slot and pattern as the preview tag and the read-only hint (`.header-note`, one line, gives up width before the glyphs, optional `.header-link`): `Not connected`, `Sign-in expired`, `Finish sign-in in your browser`, `Gmail not configured`, `Syncing…` (`Syncing first mail · N cached` during the first sync) and `Sync failed` with the cause in words when it is known: `Sync failed · no network` (a `network_unavailable` sync error; there is no "Offline" wording anywhere: offline is not a core state, only a `network_unavailable` sync error, and the user chose the failure-first wording), `Sync failed · rate limited`, `Sync failed · provider unavailable`, `Sync failed · storage unavailable`. Other or missing causes say plain `Sync failed`, so an unknown cause is never relabelled. The cause is visible words, not only a `title`. The first sync keeps its count after the cause (`Sync failed · no network · 0 cached`). **Count wording, one form per kind of place:** a standalone fact says `N conversations cached` (`1 conversation cached`), and the Account drawer says it in every state, including the first sync; the compact first-sync line, the header note (`Syncing first mail · N cached`, `Sync failed · no network · N cached`) and its twin in the empty line (`Syncing first mail… N cached.`), keeps the short `N cached` because the header has no room for the long form and the two surfaces must say the same words. The note's action link (`Connect Gmail`, `Sign in again`, `Cancel sign-in`, `Retry`) is shown **only when the empty inbox line is not already carrying the action** (one action, one place); a not-configured device has a single `Account` link, in the empty line or, when that line is not showing, in the header. **One name per action on every surface** (empty line, header link, palette, Account drawer, Provider mail note): `Connect Gmail` (disconnected only: a device that is not configured has nothing to connect with, so there is no Connect button, palette command or Provider mail link there, only `Account` and the next step), `Sign in again` (expired sign-in), `Cancel sign-in`, `Retry`, `Sync now`. **Empty-line ownership:** while the empty line shows (zero rows, plain Inbox, no reader) and says a status (every kind except the plain connected-and-synced empty text), the header note drops its visible words, link and chip, so the header shows only the Preview tag; the `account-status-note` element stays as a visually hidden `role=status` carrying the one announcement (the empty line is not a live region), so nothing is read twice and the ticking cached count is shown once, in the empty line. When rows exist, or the empty line only reports an empty inbox (a later `Syncing…` stays), the note shows as before. **No double announcement, no duplicate Retry:** while the Account drawer is open and shows the same typed sync failure as its `role=alert` (with its own Retry), the header note loses its `role=status`, hides its hidden text from assistive technology and drops its visible words and link (`drawerShowsSameFailure`); the Preview tag stays. The note returns with its words, link and announcement when the drawer closes (the empty line behind the drawer drops its own `Retry` for the same reason). A failure with no typed cause has no drawer alert, and connection notes are not repeated by it, so neither is hidden. Connection notes are not repeated by the drawer's alert, so they keep announcing. A neutral note's lead may ellipsize; the lead of a failure or an expired sign-in and the link never do, and the cause detail is whole or hidden with its dot (see the closing pass below). The detail is the note's `title` and visually hidden text and never contains the ticking cached count, so it is announced once. Nothing shows while connected and idle or in fixture mode. **Any status note, connection or sync, replaces the read-only hint** (the Account drawer covers it; the header has no room for both). The note never says actions are off: actions depend on `mutationAccess`, not on the connection, so the only standing fact it states is that cached mail stays readable. Tones: a sync failure is Coral Fault (a confirmed failure, with words), Sign-in expired is Amber Notice, the rest is Ash.
314:   - **Header width rule (follow-up to the 1030px critique).** At the 1030px floor the preview tag, the account note, the read-only hint and the `Unread only` chip used to crush the active tab to 4px (measured x=90, w=4 on the old grid). Second pass: the header grid's tab column is `minmax(min(var(--header-tabs-floor), 100%), 1fr)` with a fixed `--header-tabs-floor: 10rem` (about `Inbox 18`, the 18px gap and the `Unread only` chip), so the tab strip never drops below it; the trail column takes what is left. Third pass (the 1030px critique with a saved split, `Unread only` and the read-only hint still left `Inbox` 13px wide with no label): the floor is built from what is really in the strip, `--header-tabs-floor: max(10rem, Inbox + saved tab + chips)` with `--tab-inbox: 4.5rem` (`Inbox 18` measured 62px), `--tab-saved: 9rem` (a saved label stops at `12ch` with an ellipsis, its full name is the tab's `title`, plus the count) and `--header-chip: 4.75rem` (`Unread only` measured 73px), plus the 18px gaps, added by `:has()` rules on the header for a second tab and for each chip. Tabs and the nav are `flex: 0 0 auto`: a tab never shrinks, so a note can never take a tab's label. At 1100px and below the read-only hint collapses to its `Review access` link (the words become visually hidden, so they stay in the accessibility tree and the hover title) and the link never clips, so the hint gives up width before anything else. Estimated at 1030px (list column 718px): tabs 328px, glyphs about 190px, collapsed hint about 90px; with the browser-preview Preview tag as well (never in the native app) the hint ellipsizes first. Inside the trail the glyphs are `flex: 0 0 auto` and never shrink; the notes shrink in this order: Preview tag (`flex-shrink: 4`, but never below 5.5rem), read-only hint (`2`), account status note (`1`, link fixed). Measured in a real browser at 1030px with the worst case (first sync failed, preview, chip): tabs 160px, `Inbox 18` 62px, chip 73px, preview 96px, status 244px, glyphs unmoved; the same content on the old grid gave tabs 4px. jsdom cannot lay anything out, so the tests pin the CSS rules (the floor variables and `:has()` rules, non-shrinking tabs, the `12ch` cap, the 1100px hint collapse) and the hint, ownership and action logic (`readOnlyHintShown`, `emptyLineOwnsStatus`, `headerNoteAnnounces`, `headerNoticeAction`), not the pixels. The third-pass floor was computed from the measured widths above and the tokens, not re-measured in a browser (none was available).
